question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}y\operatorname{sin}⁡x, & 0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(-3<Y<1).$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $Y$ for $0\le y\le 2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{1}{2}y\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}y[-\operatorname{cos}⁡x]_{x=0}^{x=\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}y(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}y, & 0\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-3<Y<1) & ={\int }_{-3}^{1}{f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{2}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}({1}^{2}-{0}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
